title: Billionaires including Mark Cuban are backing a high stakes legal plot to destroy Citizens United
content:
For the first time in fifteen years, there’s a real shot at ending billionaire control of American politics and dismantling Citizens United, but not by getting it overturned.

A groundbreaking legal effort spearheaded by Harvard law professor Lawrence Lessig, backed by an unlikely coalition of billionaires like Mark Cuban and Reid Hoffman, is taking direct aim at the legal foundation that created Super PACs.

Their case doesn’t try to overturn Citizens United itself, but instead targets a lower court ruling called SpeechNow v. FEC, which unleashed unlimited political donations in 2010 and flooded elections with billionaire money.

The argument is simple: while the Supreme Court said that people can spend unlimited amounts independently, it never said billionaires can give unlimited money to political action committees especially when those contributions create the risk of corruption. Lessig and his cadre are arguing that not only has this legal precedent created a risk of corruption, corruption is rampant.

This case is now moving through the First Circuit after a bipartisan victory in Maine. Lessig and the advocates are hoping that it makes its way up to the Supreme Court, where, Lessig says that if the judges abide by an originalist interpretation of the constitution, it could finally dismantle the system that lets billionaires buy endless political power.

Basically, overturning SpeechNow would revive long-dormant laws that are already on the books capping political contributions. If Lessig’s team wins, it could mark the end of Super PACs and the beginning of a democracy that’s no longer tightly controlled by a few dozen of the richest people in America.

I’m going to be covering this legal fight very closely. Larry Lessig joined me on this week’s Free Speech Friday to break down his legal fight, where things stand, and what needs to happen next in order to win this fight.
